#### 1. cranioectodermal dysplasia 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.535)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5620924)

**Proposed mechanism:** DYNC2I1 (HGNC:18129) —DISRUPTS→ Intraflagellar transport (IFT) and dynein motor function (GO:0031090); IFT122 (HGNC:27508) —DISRUPTS→ Intraflagellar transport (IFT) and dynein motor function (GO:0031090); Intraflagellar transport (IFT) and dynein motor function (GO:0031090) —LEADS_TO→ Primary cilia assembly and function (GO:0031090); Primary cilia assembly and function (GO:0031090) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252); Primary cilia assembly and function (GO:0031090) —LEADS_TO→ Ectodermal dysplasia (HP:0001049). Mutations in DYNC2I1 and IFT122 disrupt the intraflagellar transport machinery and dynein motors, which are essential for the assembly and function of primary cilia. Defects in primary cilia lead to a cascade of downstream signaling errors, resulting in the overlapping phenotypes of microcephaly and ectodermal dysplasia.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of pathogenic variants in DYNC2I1 or IFT122 with a greater than 1% allele frequency in the gnomAD database would falsify the claim that these genes are the primary causal agents for these rare diseases. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in DYNC2I1 or IFT122 with >1% allele frequency in gnomAD)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of cilia dysfunction in these distinct rare diseases opens avenues for targeted therapeutic strategies, potentially involving modulators of cilia assembly or signaling pathways, applicable to both conditions.

#### 2. orofaciodigital syndrome 18  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.528)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5620924)

**Proposed mechanism:** DYNC2I1 (HGNC:27515) —DISRUPTS→ ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0007438); IFT57 (HGNC:28951) —DISRUPTS→ ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0007438); ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0007438) —LEADS_TO→ dental anomalies (HP:0000160); ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0007438) —LEADS_TO→ skeletal anomalies (HP:0000924); ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0007438) —LEADS_TO→ oral abnormalities (HP:0000204); ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0007438) —LEADS_TO→ limb abnormalities (HP:0001145). Loss-of-function mutations in DYNC2I1 (associated with MONDO:0014214) and IFT57 (associated with MONDO:0054770) disrupt the shared pathway of ciliary protein trafficking, leading to the convergence of dental, skeletal, oral, and limb abnormalities characteristic of both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of pathogenic variants in DYNC2I1 and IFT57 in individuals with these respective phenotypes, or the identification of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways for each disease, would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if gnomAD analysis reveals common, high-frequency variants in DYNC2I1 or IFT57 that are not associated with these phenotypes, it would weaken the causal link. _(variant: Common variants (>1%) in DYNC2I1 or IFT57 associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of disrupted ciliary protein trafficking in both Monodontic hypodontia with skeletal anomalies and Orofaciodigital syndrome 18 could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring ciliary function or mitigating downstream developmental defects, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.

#### 3. biliary, renal, neurologic, and skeletal syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.527)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5620924)

**Proposed mechanism:** DYNC2I1 (HGNC:18574) —DISRUPTS→ Ciliary function and protein transport (GO:0005983); IFT56 (HGNC:29211) —DISRUPTS→ Ciliary function and protein transport (GO:0005983); Ciliary function and protein transport (GO:0005983) —LEADS_TO→ Basement membrane organization (GO:0007095); Basement membrane organization (GO:0007095) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormality of the kidney (HP:0000077); Basement membrane organization (GO:0007095) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormality of the nervous system (HP:0012423); Basement membrane organization (GO:0007095) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0002653); Basement membrane organization (GO:0007095) —LEADS_TO→ Biliary dysgenesis (HP:0030710). Loss-of-function mutations in DYNC2I1 and IFT56 disrupt normal ciliary function and protein transport (n3). This disruption leads to impaired basement membrane organization (n4), which in turn causes the diverse phenotypic manifestations of both diseases, including renal, neurologic, skeletal, and biliary abnormalities.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of shared functional pathways or downstream effects on basement membrane organization in experimental models of DYNC2I1 and IFT56 mutations would falsify this hypothesis. Specifically, if mutations in one gene do not impact basement membrane integrity while the other does, or if the downstream phenotypes are mechanistically distinct despite shared genetic origins. _(variant: Common variants (AF > 0.01) in the coding regions of DYNC2I1 or IFT56 that are not associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving ciliary function and basement membrane integrity could reveal common therapeutic targets for both MONDO:0014214 and biliary, renal, neurologic, and skeletal syndrome, potentially leading to novel treatment strategies that address multiple organ system involvement.
